r.정치 구도: Qatar is a hereditary emirate ruled by the Al Thani family since the mid-19th century. It became independent in 1971 when British protection ended. The emir appoints the prime minister and cabinet, and political parties are not allowed. The 2003 constitution provided for 30 of the 45 members of the advisory Shura Council to be elected, but the first vote was not held until 2021. Some tribes were excluded from voting, which caused friction, and in a November 2024 referendum more than 90% backed scrapping the elections, so the emir again appoints every member. Citizens make up only about one in ten residents. Gas income pays for generous jobs and benefits for them, and that bargain underpins the system. The treatment of the foreign workers who do most construction and service jobs drew international criticism before the 2022 World Cup, and reforms in 2020 let workers change jobs without their employer's permission and set a minimum wage.

t.why: The offshore North Field, shared with Iran, is the largest gas field in the world. Qatar turns that gas into liquefied natural gas and ranks with the United States and Australia as one of the top three exporters. Al Udeid Air Base near Doha is the largest US base in the Middle East, yet Qatar also hosts offices of the Taliban and Hamas, which is why the 2020 US-Taliban agreement and the Gaza ceasefire talks took place in Doha. A small state among large neighbors, it chose to be the place where everyone can talk. That independent line cost it in 2017, when Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and others cut ties and blockaded it for three and a half years. Being a mediator has not kept it safe either. Iran fired missiles at Al Udeid in June 2025, and that September Israel struck Hamas leaders in Doha. In the 2026 war between the United States, Israel and Iran, Iranian missiles hit Qatar repeatedly, and in March strikes on the Ras Laffan gas complex knocked out about a sixth of its export capacity. With the Strait of Hormuz closed as well, it declared force majeure on long-term supply contracts with several countries. Since then it has mediated between Washington and Tehran alongside Pakistan.
t.rel: Small but a big gas exporter. It keeps channels open even to Hamas and the Taliban and often mediates, and from 2017 to 2021 it was cut off and blockaded by Saudi Arabia and other neighbors.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1974. Korea Gas Corporation has bought Qatari gas under long-term contracts since the late 1990s, making Qatar one of South Korea's major suppliers of liquefied natural gas. In 2021 it signed a new deal for 2 million tons a year for 20 years starting in 2025. The ships that carry the gas are built in South Korea too: between 2022 and 2024 QatarEnergy ordered 98 LNG carriers from the three big Korean shipbuilders. The National Museum of Qatar in Doha was built by Hyundai Engineering & Construction. After the attack on Ras Laffan in March 2026, long-term cargoes bound for South Korea were among those covered by force majeure, and Seoul has asked Qatar to give Korean volumes priority once production and shipping recover.
t.know: Foreign workers far outnumber citizens, who make up just over 10% of the population.
etext: The North Field lies under shallow water and its gas is concentrated in one place, so production costs are among the lowest in the world. State-owned QatarEnergy liquefies the gas at Ras Laffan and ships it out. Helium recovered alongside the gas supplies about a third of the world market. An expansion was under way to nearly double export capacity by 2030, but after the 2026 attacks part of the existing plant will take years to repair.

The Qatar Investment Authority, a sovereign wealth fund set up in 2005, invests gas income abroad. It holds stakes in Volkswagen, Barclays and Heathrow Airport and owns Harrods in London outright. It is also the cushion that carries the country through periods when gas cannot be sold.

Qatar Airways and Hamad International Airport draw transfer passengers between Europe and Asia, and the 2022 World Cup was the occasion to build a metro, stadiums and hotels. These were investments in being known for something besides gas.

Its gas plant is concentrated at one site, Ras Laffan, and the only way out for ships is the Strait of Hormuz. Unlike some neighbors it has no pipeline around the strait. The 2026 war exposed both at once. With so few citizens, private-sector jobs are filled almost entirely by foreigners.
